title: Hosted API optimistic tool-resolve playbook
abstract: Brainstorm + lightweight PRD sketch for an optimistic tool resolution mode in the Hosted API SDK and streaming surface. Goal: let clients speculatively render actions and partial structured results while server-side validation/execute completes, improving perceived latency and developer ergonomics without breaking determinism for critical flows.
problem_statement: Users building interactive UIs (chat assistants, IDE helpers, search augmenters) frequently want to surface actionable content immediately while the backend runs slow or calls external tools. Current patterns either: (a) block and wait for server-confirmed tool outputs (safer but high latency), or (b) show unverified text fragments (fast but error-prone and hard to reconcile). We need a product surface that provides low-latency optimistic interactions with clear reconciliation semantics and SDK ergonomics for adoption.
goals: 1) Provide an SDK-first optimistic execution mode for streaming responses and tool calls that is safe-by-default and easy to adopt. 2) Define protocol-level frames for speculative outputs, confirmation messages, and reconciliation deltas. 3) Offer telemetry hooks for tracing optimistic paths, reconciliation success/failure rates, and user-visible regressions. 4) Keep server authoritative so final state is always explicit and auditable.
non_goals: 1) Not introducing a new persistence layer for long-running tool workflows (we rely on existing session storage). 2) Not changing underlying model semantics; this is a serving/contract feature. 3) Not building a full UI library — focus on SDK primitives and wire protocol.
solution_overview: Introduce an 'optimistic' delivery channel in streaming responses: the model/runtime can emit 'speculative frames' that are labeled and schema-typed. The client SDK exposes these as transient events (onSpeculativeFrame) and can optionally apply deterministic heuristics to convert them to UI actions. When the server completes tool execution or authoritative validation, it emits a 'confirmation' frame that either: (a) confirms the speculative content (idempotent commit), (b) emits a delta patch to adjust fields, or (c) emits a rollback instruction. The SDK supports automatic reconciliation strategies (auto-apply, preview-only, manual-accept) and exposes hooks for telemetry and user prompts.
api_contract_sketch:
- Response stream frames carry a 'frame_type' header: speculative | confirm | patch | rollback | progress.
- Each frame has a 'spec_id' UUID when speculative (ties speculative frames to later confirmations).
- Structured payloads follow a schema field: {schema_version, schema_name, payload}. The SDK uses schema_name to validate and surface typed objects.
- Tool-call frames include metadata: {tool_name, call_args, estimated_confidence, timeout_hint}. Speculative frames may omit final tool outputs but include 'intent' and 'preview' fields.
- Confirm frames include 'final_payload' and an ordered list of 'patches' (ops: replace, insert, remove) for minimal updates.
- Rollback frames include reason codes (validation_error, tool_failure, capacity_fallback).
- Backpressure: clients send optional 'client_window' updates signaling how many speculative frames they can safely render; server uses this to throttle speculative emissions.
sdk_ergonomics_notes:
- JS SDK: expose a StreamingResponse async iterator that yields objects of shape {type: 'speculative'|'confirm'|'patch'|'rollback'|'progress', spec_id, schema, payload, meta}.
- Provide helpers: applySpeculative(frame) returns an opaque 'applyToken' that can be used to reconcile or revert UI diffs.
- Async UI pattern: renderPreview(frame) -> show 'unverified' badge; onConfirm -> replace badge with authoritative content; onRollback -> highlight changes and offer accept/retry buttons.
- Default strategy: preview-only for text content; auto-apply for small deterministic edits (e.g., formatting, fillers) when estimated_confidence > 0.9.
- Mobile considerations: enable a compact preview mode; memory/timeouts tuned to avoid long-lived speculative state on low-memory clients.
- Local validation: SDK ships with JSON-schema shallow validation for payloads to avoid obviously malformed speculative frames being applied.
- Cancellation: expose CancellationToken to cancel pending speculative frames and associated tool calls; server must honor cancellations but may still emit confirmation/rollback for in-flight operations.
- Developer ergonomics: small, composable primitives (onSpeculative, onConfirm, onPatch, applyPreview, revertPreview, telemetry hooks) rather than a monolithic opinionated flow.
telemetry_and_observability:
- Important metrics: speculative_emit_rate, speculative_confirm_rate, speculative_rollback_rate, avg_time_to_confirmation, user_visible_regression_rate, speculative_bytes_per_session.
- Traces: associate speculative frames, confirm frames, and tool-execution spans with a single request_id and spec_id.
- Logging: servers log reason codes for rollbacks and confidence estimates for later ML analysis.
- Alerts: create SLOs around speculative_confirm_rate for high-value customers; if rollback rate > 10% for a route, trigger QA review.
- Dashboard surfaces: per-route speculative vs authoritative latencies, distribution of confidence estimates, top rollback reasons, SDK versions and adoption.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal preview): implement server frame headers and JS SDK hooks; use with 2 internal teams (console assistant and demos). Phase 1 (beta): opt-in flag for selected customers, telemetry collection, simple reconciliation defaults. Phase 2 (general availability): SDK stable APIs, mobile SDKs updated, docs and migration guide, opt-out grace period. Phase 3: add server-side heuristics for automatic speculative suppression when capacity constrained and add per-customer policy controls.
risks_and_open_questions:
- UX risk: users might be confused by transient speculative content — need clear visual affordances.
- Complexity risk: increased surface area in SDKs and runtime for handling reconciliation; potential for subtle bugs around patch ordering.
- Determinism vs speed: which kinds of content should we never allow speculative auto-apply for (financial/legal statements, PII edits)? Need policy list.
- Security: ensure speculative frames cannot leak internal-only tool outputs (e.g., debug traces).
- Billing/SLAs: should speculative frames count toward usage billing? They are generated server-side and consume compute; proposed: bill by final confirmed tokens, but track speculative compute separately for capacity planning.
- Open question: tightness of schema_versioning — do we require server SDK compatibility checks before emitting speculative frames?
- Edge case: if client disconnects before confirmation, should final confirmation be retried/delivered via webhook or stored for later session reconciliation?
integration_checklist:
- Short-term: add spec_id to existing streaming protocol, add frame_type enum, implement basic JS SDK hooks, add telemetry tags, instrument two internal apps.
- Medium-term: add mobile SDK parity, add server-side gating by confidence, build reconciliation UI patterns and example components, update docs and migration guide.
- Long-term: policy dashboard for admins to configure auto-apply rules, integrate with Redwood Console rollouts and experiment tracking.
acceptance_criteria:
- SDK exposes the streaming frame types and simple reconciliation helpers documented in the API sketch.
- Internal teams report measurable perceived latency improvement (>=15% median time-to-first-action) on flows that adopt optimistic mode.
- Rollback rate < 8% on internal beta routes after two weeks of telemetry.
- Telemetry primitives emit request_id+spec_id traces for 95% of speculative events.
- Documentation and migration guide published before beta.
open_todos:
- Decide billing treatment for speculative frames (ENG + Finance).
- Create a short UI kit for optimistic previews and rollback affordances (Design).
- Draft policy list for never-auto-apply content (Legal + Product).
- Implement lightweight JSON-schema validator in SDK (Eng).
- Wire up trace propagation for mobile SDKs (SRE + Mobile Eng).
